title: Simulation Task
description: Develop a multi-agent simulation system that models the spread of mask-wearing behavior through social networks.
simulation_focus: Predict agents' mask-wearing behavior over day 30 - day 39 (last ten days) based on their attributes, social connections, and past behavior
Model information propagation and behavioral changes triggered by social influence and government intervention starting on Day 10

data_files.agent_attributes.csv: Contains demographic and behavioral attributes of each agent, including age, occupation, risk perception, and social connection counts
data_files.social_network.json: Contains structured data representing a social network. Each entry corresponds to a user (identified by a unique integer ID), and the values describe the different types of relationships that user has with others. Data Structure: The top-level structure is a dictionary ({} in JSON). Keys: Each key is a unique user ID (as an integer, e.g., 0, 1, 2, etc.). Values: Each value is another dictionary with the following fields: "family": a list of user IDs representing family connections. "work_school": a list of user IDs representing colleagues or schoolmates. "community": a list of user IDs representing community-level acquaintances. "all": a merged list of all user IDs connected to the user across the three categories above.
data_files.train_data.csv: Time series data for the first 30 days, used for training the model

RMSE.description: Root Mean Square Error measuring overall predictive accuracy of mask adoption rates
RMSE.interpretation: Directly interpretable as percentage deviations due to the 0-1 range

overall_simulation_design.rationale: The goal is to model and experiment with how mask-wearing behavior diffuses through a social network and to test interventions (e.g., targeted information campaigns, mandates, seeding strategies). The data provide initial states, agent heterogeneity, and a multiplex network suitable for counterfactual intervention scenarios.
overall_simulation_design.initialization: 1) Load agent_attributes.csv to instantiate one agent per row with demographics, risk_perception, and initial_mask_wearing. 2) Build multiplex graphs (family, work_school, community) from social_network.json. 3) Set initial wearing_mask either from agent_attributes.initial_mask_wearing or, if train_data.csv is present, override with day 0 wearing_mask where available. 4) Initialize received_info from train_data day 0 where available; otherwise seed from exogenous info rates. 5) Set parameter values (influence weights, info rates, inertia, etc.) from calibration or scenario inputs.
outputs: per-agent daily trajectories: wearing_mask(t), received_info(t), exposure_by_layer(t)
aggregate adoption curves overall and by subgroup (age_group, occupation, layer degree quantiles)
intervention logs (when/where info injected, mandates applied)
calibration diagnostics (fitted parameters, likelihood/metric scores, transition matrices)
network-level analytics (degree/centrality distributions, layer-wise contact summaries)

scale_granularity.population_size: Number of unique agent_ids in social_network.json (≈ 1,000 in example), cross-validated with agent_attributes.csv row count
scale_granularity.rationale: train_data.csv is daily; mask-wearing and information exposure change on day-level cadence. No explicit geography is provided; interactions are captured via the multiplex network.

agent_archetypes.construction_from_data: Map each CSV row to an agent. role derivation: Student -> Student; occupation Blue Collar -> Worker_Blue; White Collar -> Worker_White; else use age_group to assign Other (e.g., Youth not in workforce). Initialize wearing_mask from agent_attributes.initial_mask_wearing unless train_data day 0 exists for that agent; if both present, prefer train_data day 0. Set layer degree targets from family/work_school/community columns (for validation).
agent_archetypes.update_from_data: Use train_data.csv to estimate transition models: P(mask_t=1 | mask_{t-1}, received_info_t, received_info_{t-1}) and relapse P(mask_t=0 | mask_{t-1}=1, signals). Fit logistic/Markov transition parameters and layer weights by aligning simulated exposures with observed adoption trajectories during training period.

interaction_topology.construction_from_data: Read social_network.json; convert keys to ints; deduplicate neighbors per layer; optionally enforce undirected symmetry by adding reciprocal edges if missing. Validate that degree per layer approximates agent_attributes counts (use counts diagnostically; trust explicit edges for simulation). Use 'all' only for aggregate analyses; primary diffusion uses explicit family, work_school, community layers.

information_propagation.topology: family, work_school, community layers (independent-cascade with layer-specific rates)
information_propagation.mechanism: Each day, informed agents (received_info==1 today or with memory_info>0) attempt to inform neighbors on each layer with probability info_rate_layer. Information can also be seeded exogenously (media) with a global rate or targeted by role/degree. memory_info decays geometrically by memory_decay each day.
information_propagation.construction_from_data: Use train_data.received_info frequencies to calibrate info_rate_layer and exogenous media rate so that simulated per-day info incidence matches observed during the training window. Initialize informed seeds on day 0 using train_data where available.

parameters.notes: Estimate initial values by matching observed daily received_info prevalence and autocorrelation; refine via calibration to minimize error on adoption transitions.

exogenous_signals.name: media_campaign_intensity
exogenous_signals.construction_from_data: Fit to match residual received_info after accounting for neighbor-to-neighbor diffusion in train_data (or set by scenario).
exogenous_signals.effect_on_agents: Adds to probability of received_info on a given day (Bernoulli with media_info_rate_global).

exogenous_signals.name: mask_mandate_intensity
exogenous_signals.construction_from_data: Scenario input (not provided in data); used in what-if/policy runs.
exogenous_signals.effect_on_agents: Adds to adoption utility/log-odds directly; can also reduce relapse probability.

exogenous_signals.name: targeted_seeding
exogenous_signals.construction_from_data: Scenario input: select seed sets by role, degree, or centrality computed from social_network.
exogenous_signals.effect_on_agents: Set received_info=1 and optionally wearing_mask=1 with a compliance probability.

Student.policy_form: Logistic adoption with inertia and layer-weighted peer influence: logit P(mask_t=1) = b0 + b_inertia*mask_{t-1} + wF*frac_masked_family + wW*frac_masked_work_school + wC*frac_masked_community + bInfo*(received_info_t + alpha*memory_info) + bRisk*risk_perception + bMandate*mask_mandate_intensity. If mask_{t-1}=1, relapse probability is modeled via separate logit with its own parameters.

Worker_Blue.policy_form: Same logistic form; allow role-specific layer weights (often higher community influence).

Worker_White.policy_form: Same logistic form; allow different wW and wC to capture workplace-centric influence.

Other (Youth/Retired/Unemployed).policy_form: Same logistic form; emphasize family and community influence; possibly lower inertia for Youth.

holdout_plan.train_range: First 80% of days per agent: day 0 to floor(0.8*T)-1, where T is max day+1 in train_data for that agent
holdout_plan.validation_range: Last 20% of days per agent: day floor(0.8*T) to T-1
holdout_plan.notes: Optionally also hold out 10% of agents entirely for external validation of generalization across network positions. Ensure no leakage of validation-period exogenous settings into training.

metrics.name: RMSE_aggregate
metrics.definition: RMSE between simulated and observed daily mask adoption rates (overall and by role) on validation days.

metrics.name: MAE_aggregate
metrics.definition: MAE between simulated and observed adoption curves over validation days.

metrics.name: Brier
metrics.definition: Brier score of per-agent predicted probabilities of wearing_mask on validation days.

metrics.name: TransitionFit
metrics.definition: Absolute/relative error between observed and simulated transition probabilities P01, P11, P10 by role and layer-exposure deciles.

simulation_evaluation.comparison_method: Run multiple stochastic simulation replicates; average outputs and compute confidence intervals. Align simulated days with validation days; compute metrics overall and stratified by occupation/age_group. Report tables and curves; select parameters by minimizing RMSE_aggregate with TransitionFit as constraint.

calibratable_parameters.name: influence_weight_family
calibratable_parameters.source: Layered social influence; constrained by family degree and observed diffusion speed in train_data
calibratable_parameters.notes: Higher family weight increases clustering-driven adoption.

calibratable_parameters.name: influence_weight_work_school
calibratable_parameters.notes: Role-specific tuning for Students and Workers.

calibratable_parameters.name: influence_weight_community
calibratable_parameters.source: Community layer influence; typically lower than family/work

calibratable_parameters.name: baseline_adoption_bias
calibratable_parameters.source: Intercept of logistic adoption; learned from overall adoption level

calibratable_parameters.name: inertia_weight
calibratable_parameters.source: Persistence of mask-wearing from day to day

calibratable_parameters.name: info_effect_weight
calibratable_parameters.source: Effect of received_info on adoption probability
calibratable_parameters.notes: Estimated from co-occurrence of info and adoption in train_data.

calibratable_parameters.name: info_rate_family|work_school|community
calibratable_parameters.notes: Fit to match observed received_info incidence and timing.

calibratable_parameters.name: risk_weight
calibratable_parameters.source: Scales impact of risk_perception on adoption

calibratable_parameters.name: mandate_effect_weight
calibratable_parameters.source: Policy strength mapping to adoption utility

calibratable_parameters.name: relapse_bias
calibratable_parameters.source: Baseline propensity to stop wearing once adopted

file_summaries.semantic_summary:
Semantic metadata summary for agent_attributes.csv (for mask-wearing diffusion simulation)

Overall data structure and type
- Format: Tabular CSV; one row per agent; primary key: agent_id (integer).
- Columns and types:
  - age (int), age_group (categorical), occupation (categorical)
  - risk_perception (float in [0,1])
  - initial_mask_wearing (boolean)
  - family_connections, work_school_connections, community_connections, total_connections (ints)
- Population size = number of rows; provides initial state and heterogeneity.

Relationships or nested elements
- No explicit nesting; relationships are implicit via multilayer degree counts:
  - Three network layers: family, work/school, community.
  - total_connections ≈ family + work_school + community (use for validation).
- No edge list provided; only degree targets per layer. Network topology must be generated to satisfy these degree sequences and layer semantics.
- Occupation and age_group imply layer membership patterns (e.g., Students to school layer; Blue/White Collar to work layer; Youth likely in family/school).

How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions
- Agent construction:
  - Each row becomes an Agent with attributes: demographics, risk_perception, initial_mask_wearing.
  - initial_mask_wearing sets the initial behavioral state (seed adopters).
  - risk_perception informs adoption propensity/threshold or baseline probability.
- Network generation:
  - Build three graphs (family, work/school, community) per the degree counts.
  - Assign agents to households and workplaces/schools consistent with age_group and occupation; connect within groups to meet degree targets; fill remaining with community edges.
  - Optionally weight layers differently (e.g., family > work/school > community) in influence calculations.
- Interaction dynamics:
  - At each timestep, update mask-wearing based on social influence from neighbors across layers (weighted by layer) and agent risk_perception.
  - Age_group/occupation can modulate susceptibility, influence strength, or mixing assortativity.
  - Use total_connections to compute exposure/normalized neighbor fractions.
- Validation and constraints:
  - Check total_connections equals the sum of layer degrees.
  - Ensure risk_perception within [0,1]; boolean parsing for initial_mask_wearing.
  - Calibrate network generation to preserve degree distributions and group structures implied by age/occupation.

Semantic metadata summary for social_network.json (mask-wearing diffusion simulation)

Overall data structure and type
- JSON object mapping agent IDs (as strings) to adjacency lists (dictionary per agent).
- Scale appears to be ~1,000 agents (IDs 0–999 observed).
- Each agent record contains four arrays of integers (neighbor IDs): family, work_school, community, and all.

Relationships or nested elements
- Multiplex (layered) social network:
  - family: close-kin ties.
  - work_school: workplace/school ties.
  - community: broader community ties.
  - all: union of the three layers (appears deduplicated), useful for single-layer analyses.
- Adjacency lists imply edges from the focal agent to listed neighbor IDs. Reciprocity is not guaranteed by the format; treat edges as directed unless you enforce symmetry during preprocessing.
- Overlap across layers is possible (same neighbor appearing in multiple layers), implying stronger composite relationships if aggregated.
- Keys are strings; neighbor IDs are integers—convert consistently to a single type when building graphs.

How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions
- Agents: one agent per top-level key; agent state includes mask-wearing status (binary or probabilistic), susceptibility to influence, and possibly layer-specific responsiveness.
- Networks:
  - Build a separate graph per layer (family, work_school, community) to model layer-specific contact rates and influence strengths.
  - Optionally build an aggregated graph from all for simplified simulations; if aggregating, weight edges by layer (e.g., family > work_school > community) and by multiplicity (appearances across layers).
- Interaction scheduling:
  - Time-stepped contacts sampled per layer using layer-specific frequencies (e.g., daily family/work, less frequent community).
  - Influence model choices: linear threshold, independent cascade, or weighted social reinforcement; use layer weights to modulate adoption probabilities.
- Parameterization suggestions:
  - Higher influence/weight for family edges; moderate for work_school; lower for community.
  - Consider directed vs. undirected handling: default to undirected for symmetric social influence unless data validation shows strong asymmetry.
- Preprocessing checks:
  - Convert keys to ints; validate that all referenced neighbor IDs exist as nodes.
  - Deduplicate neighbors within layers; ensure all is truly the union.
  - Optionally enforce symmetry to create undirected graphs for influence processes.
- Metrics for seeding/analysis:
  - Compute degree/centrality per layer to choose initial mask adopters or target interventions.
  - Track layer-specific adoption curves to assess where behavior spreads fastest.

Semantic metadata summary for train_data.csv

- Overall structure and type
  - Format: Tabular CSV; one row per agent-day observation (longitudinal/panel data).
  - Columns:
    - day: integer time step (discrete daily index).
    - agent_id: integer agent identifier (keys multiple rows per agent across days).
    - wearing_mask: boolean state of the agent that day.
    - received_info: boolean indicating whether agent received pro-mask information that day.

- Relationships and nesting
  - No nested elements; fully flat schema.
  - Implicit relationships:
    - Temporal linkage: rows with same agent_id ordered by day form a time series trajectory.
    - State transitions: wearing_mask at day t depends on prior states and possibly received_info at day t (or t-1, depending on chosen update rule).
  - Relational join potential: agent_id can link to separate datasets (e.g., network edges, demographics) not present here.

- How this data should inform simulation entities and interactions
  - Agents: initialize each agent with time-evolving state variables wearing_mask and received_info.
  - Dynamics calibration:
    - Estimate transition probabilities/hazards such as P(mask_t = 1 | mask_{t-1}, received_info_t, received_info_{t-1}) and relapse rates P(mask_t = 0 | mask_{t-1} = 1).
    - Infer persistence/memory effects and spontaneous adoption without information.
  - Time step: daily synchronous/asynchronous updates aligned to the day field.
  - Information process: received_info is an exogenous/endogenous event flag to be generated via the social network in the simulation; use observed co-occurrence with mask adoption to parameterize influence strength.
  - Validation: compare simulated panel trajectories (per agent) to empirical distributions of adoption, duration, and switching patterns from this file.
  - Note: Network topology is not included; must be supplied separately and connected via agent_id to drive received_info propagation.
